properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Both reports arrived at this from opposite directions on 2026-08-31, neither connecting it to the other.

· **bhome (part 6), on cost.** A refused bulk write meant re-sending a ~4 KB decision body verbatim, because nothing was created. "Field-level validation before the write, or a dry-run, would make long-prose nodes cheaper to get right. This is the same underlying gap as the append-vs-replace friction: reflow2 has no way to say 'change this one thing' on a large node."
· **musicjug (idea 2), on safety.** The revision reply says, correctly, that it holds the only copy in existence of the replaced field — so it is the one caller that could still save it. "Snapshot automatically, or offer `snapshot_prior: true`, and the warning becomes a receipt rather than a regret."

THREE IDEAS: a **dry run** (validate without writing); **`snapshot_prior: true`** (keep what is being replaced); **field-level validation** before the write is attempted.

📌 PART OF THIS IS ALREADY TRUE AND WAS NOT KNOWN TO EITHER REPORTER: the `add_*` constructors take content fields as REQUIRED TO CREATE AND OPTIONAL TO REVISE — call again with the same id and only what you are changing, and omitted fields keep their stored value. So "change this one thing" exists for those. It does NOT exist for `create_node`, which merges but where a partial props object is the ordinary path, and the cost bhome hit was a REFUSED bulk write, where the issue is that a refusal discards work rather than that an update needs the whole node.

⚠️ SO THE THREE ASKS ARE NOT EQUALLY MOTIVATED, and it is worth separating them before building any: the partial-update ask is largely already answered and the instruction may simply be unfindable; the dry-run ask is about refusals discarding a large payload; the snapshot ask is about a value being lost. Only the third is a data-loss risk, and it is the one with a named cheap fix.

⚠️ AND ON THE SEQUENCING POINT UNDERNEATH musicjug's version: "the prescribed order is not reliably achievable from a harness that emits parallel tool batches." A rule that depends on call ORDER can be broken by an agent host without either party choosing to, which is an argument for the tool preserving the value itself rather than instructing the caller to.
properties.name: OPEN — should a write offer a dry run, a snapshot-on-revise, or field-level validation, so a large node is not re-sent whole to change one thing?
properties.rationale: Two reports, two directions, one underlying question. The note that partial revision already exists for the `add_*` constructors is from this project's own tool descriptions and was available to neither reporter — which is itself a finding about discoverability.
